title: Defaulting Missing Metrics to Zero (Downward Bias)
pattern: Using `unwrap_or(0)` or defaulting null/missing metric readings to `0` when computing statistical averages.
why_bad: Defaulting missing data points to zero introduces a massive artificial downward bias in the average. If 50% of metric packets are lost, the average download speed reported will be cut in half, falsely representing a network speed issue rather than a packet-reporting loss issue.
detection: Look for default values of `0` used on telemetry variables before computing averages or quotients.
counterexample: `Context-dependent`. If `0` is the actual, physically verified state of the missed value, it is correct.
strength: Strong` — mathematically injects downward bias proportional to data loss.
source: Trevor Foucher & Dustin Boswell - *The Art of Readable Code* (2012), Chapter 15, p. 219.
